text: Gordon Palm does it again. So I wanna make a video discussing Gordon Palm. I've had a couple of people ask me about this and I kinda wanted to shed my thoughts on something like this. So fundamentally all Gordon Palm is is just Ken Palm's numbers of tempo and offensive efficiency plotted on some weird graph that should look like this. So this is what this graph is. You have tempo on the x-axis where fast teams are over here, slow teams are over here, and then on the y-axis you have their offensive efficiency which is the number of points scored per 100 possessions and is calculated using the four factors which are effective field goal percentage, rebounds, turnover percentage, and free throw rate. Now the biggest problem I have with this method or whatever you wanna call it, system, is it ignores pretty much all of the data, right? He's gonna tell you that Alabama won. Alabama and UNC are way faster than average and how is Gordon Palm, quote unquote, the rate and efficiency have something to do with a team that was better offensively beating a team that was a little worse offensively? To me it wasn't pace that necessarily did that, that was offensive efficiency that did that. But it also ignores pretty much every single upset that's happened. UK in his elite quadrant lost two. Where is Oakland? Right there in the bad quadrant. Yale upset UConn. I mean, we've seen this over and over where these slow teams can slow these really, really, really fast teams down enough and limit the number of possessions and they hit enough threes and voila, an upset happens. I mean, it would be really difficult to ignore that UConn is playing kind of lights out right now and they're the most efficient offense. So how do you reconcile something like this? Efficiency and pace, when combined one another, sure they can be a lethal combination, but you've seen other, I don't even call them systems, but descriptions of pace and efficiency. You've heard Ryan Hammer talk about of his trapezoid of excellence, which is a lot better in my opinion than Gordon Palm, why? Because really all it is is describing teams that are very efficient per 100 possessions and they have a variability in pace in which they do that. Some teams faster, some teams slower. But ultimately, as long as they are very efficient with their possessions, that is to me what is leading to wins and points scored. Now looking at only the sweet 16 of this Gordon Palm type of graph, which again, tempo and offensive efficiency, you see this exact phenomenon happened last night. The slower paced team actually was able to limit the number of possessions of a better, more efficient team that plays faster and they won, right? So I really wanna point this out, it's a cherry picks. The other thing, we put together a model using all pre-tournament data from 2001 all the way through 2023 to look and predict the probability of each team winning the championship. And we can show statistically that tempo is a non-significant variable in the model. What does that mean? It means that there is no statistical certainty, so to speak, relationship between tempo and winning the championship. And to me, why is that? It's because you can have a varying amount of quote unquote tempo or pace, but your offensive efficiency is way more important, aka how efficient you are given that pace and the efficiency trumps the pace. Personally, I think you're way better off using offensive and defensive efficiency. These are way, way more predictive. They are actually tempo adjusted in Ken Palm's numbers for both offensive defense. And this is going to give you a way better, more predictive idea overall on how teams are gonna do. And using models that actually use the four factor from all of the play-by-play data, Ken Palm is obviously doing that, Bart Torvik does that, you can even use Massey ratings to do that, are going to get you a lot closer at that idea than just using one sliver and then extrapolating that variable, i.e. tempo, as the cause of all things. That's just going to fall short a lot of the time. But let me know in the comments, does Gordon Palm have a shot and have you been using it to make money or has it been losing money? I haven't followed closely, but it just seems like it ignores a lot of the data. Let me know.
